organization: Center for Independence of the Disabled, New York
program: Disability benefits navigation, community transitions, mental-health support and advocacy

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-sixth-seventh-independent-acceptance.json: primary-source checks, independent reconstruction of every scenario, and explicit uncertainty review; accepted as conditional alpha modeling, not measured causal impact.

priceScope: Illustrative marginal unrestricted gift; selected direct-service health pathways within whole-organization costs

what: CIDNY helps people with disabilities obtain benefits, navigate care and move into community living.
It also provides peer mental-health support and advocates for accessibility and disability rights.
Our very uncertain, conditional estimate is $59.5 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs for the quantified pathways within whole-recipient costs.
strengths: Program-level reporting makes a conservative, unsummed transition cohort identifiable.
Disability-led service delivery addresses practical barriers to using publicly financed care.
Original returns and annual summaries provide a traceable financial baseline.
reservations: Transition totals conflict and program overlap is unresolved.
Health utility, counterfactual success and marginal funding responsiveness are subjective priors.
Public contracts dominate funding, and broader advocacy outcomes remain unpriced.

sections.what: The charitable recipient is Center for Independence of the Disabled in New York, Inc., EIN 13-2984549, distinct from CIDNY Independent Living Services. Its mix includes navigation, transition coordination, ombudsman work, peer support and policy advocacy. The model retains all functions in the expense denominator. [Official program and financial index](https://www.cidny.org/annual-reports/)
sections.monitoring: The supplied primary-source audit records 132 Open Doors transitions, 225 Housing Services transitions and a conflicting 387 president's aggregate. We use only 132; none of the others are added. CBT has 27 unique participants, but reported survey improvement is uncontrolled and response-selected. The 65,000 reach claim and assistance contacts are not clinical beneficiaries. The model requests unique IDs across programs, baseline status, actual additional care, six- and twelve-month health measurement, and unsuccessful cases. [FY25 report](https://www.cidny.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/CIDNY-2024-25-Annual-Report.pdf)
sections.qualitative: Moving to a preferred community setting can improve autonomy, while navigation can make existing health benefits usable. The national MFP evaluation follows 803 survey completers before and one year after transition; it supports plausibility, but neither a randomized CIDNY effect nor an EQ-5D utility increment. Our 0.05 transition utility is therefore a judgment, not that study's measurement. No disability cure, survival gain or lifetime credit is assumed. [Original evaluator description](https://www.mathematica.org/publications/money-follows-the-person-change-in-participant-experience-during-the-first-year-of-community-living)
sections.cost: The central conditional estimate is $59.5 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs (0.00016808 QALYs per $1,000). For a $1,000 unrestricted gift, annual output-to-whole-expense ratios are scaled by a 0.5 capacity elasticity, then counterfactual success and finite health gains. Central annual-equivalent inputs are 132 transitions, 708 care-navigation consumers and 27 CBT participants; success fractions 0.3/.2/.3, annual utilities 0.05/.02/.05, and durations 1.5/.5/.5 years. Navigation and CBT receive 0.8 and 0.5 residual-overlap multipliers. Mortality is an assumed 5% annually for transitions, 2% navigation and 1% CBT; benefits start after 0.25 years and discount 3%. Additional community time ends when alternatives catch up. Other portfolio net health is zero as a provisional accounting convention, not proof of no benefit or a lower bound. The formula and every scenario override are serialized.
sections.funding: Annual-summary FY2023/2024/2025 expenses are $8,937,955/$9,831,086/$11,736,265, a descriptive mean of $10,168,435.33. Latest expense includes program $10,283,988, management $1,349,456 and fundraising $102,821. Original FY2023 Form 990 confirms $8,937,955; FY2022 original shows $8,292,256. The website's '2024' return is an image PDF not successfully read here: three original comparable recent returns are NOT verified. FY2023's annual-summary stale footnote is superseded for that amount by its original return. FY24/25 remain annual-report financial approximations. FY25 government contracts $9,643,944 and veterans revenue $1,656,969 make full gift additionality implausible without a staffing constraint; 0.5 elasticity is deliberately contestable. Public care and housing costs are outside donor costs. [FY2023 original return](https://www.cidny.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/CIDNY-06_30_23-990-V1-Public-Disclosure-Copy-CENTER-FOR-INDEP.-OF-THE-DISBLED-IN-NY.pdf)

model.costScope: $1000 unrestricted donor cost; whole-recipient FY25 annual expense calibrates output scaling. Public treatment/housing expenditures and unrecognized volunteer resources excluded; not full social cost-effectiveness.
model.geographicAttribution: g=1 for these modeled five-borough pathways within OMB23-01 NYC MSA; statewide advocacy excluded. This is not all-recipient benefit allocation.
model.formula: For pathway j: k=ln(1+d)-ln(1-m_j); F_j=exp(-k*lag_j)*(1-exp(-k*T_j))/k (T if k=0). Qall=(D/C)*b*sum(N_j*r_j*u_j*F_j*o_j)-h; Qedition=(D/C)*b*sum(N_j*r_j*u_j*F_j*o_j*g_j)-h*gH. Price10=10*D/Qedition if positive.
model.counterfactual: Existing contracts, transition subsidies, other navigators and clinical providers continue. r is the fraction whose meaningful outcome is changed versus those alternatives; duration is only time gained before convergence. b removes grant replacement and capacity constraints.
model.attribution: b=.5 is marginal output elasticity relative to historical average productivity, not a claimed unrestricted program allocation. Whole-recipient expenditure stays in C. No policy credit added.
model.uncertainty: Very weak confidence. Source-observed service counts are anchors, not causal effects; r,u,T,b,o and mortality are subjective. Null and negative outcomes are plausible.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional transitions accelerated, actual care access improved, and CBT response beyond alternatives; these map to finite incremental health utility.

inputs.rationale: All-recipient FY25 annual-summary expense.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Half of historical output per dollar survives substitution and marginal capacity limits; no measured fundraising elasticity.

inputs.name: d
inputs.rationale: Explicit time preference, sensitivity 0–5%.

inputs.name: h
inputs.rationale: Other net health provisionally zero; adverse scenario allows loss outside benefit multipliers.

inputs.name: gH
inputs.rationale: Modeled adverse harm local.
